description: [FREE: 25 calls/day, then $0.01 USDC per call via x402] Before your agent sends a figure to a customer, a ledger or another agent, check it. Each claim is an expression and the value you believe it equals: plain arithmetic ("1299.99 * 3 * 1.0825" expected "4221.87") or over your rows ("sum([Amount])" expected "4312.50", with optional per-claim where filters). Answers per claim: "correct" (exactly equal, or within your tolerance), "correct_when_rounded" (equal once the true value is rounded half-up to the decimals you wrote), or "wrong", always with the exact value and the difference. Same exact engine as table_calc and decimal_calc; up to 50 claims per call, with a receipt you can attach as proof.

asOf.description: the date age_days() counts up to, YYYY-MM-DD (required for age_days: answers never silently depend on today's date)

expected.description: the value to check, as a decimal string; $, commas and % are read

expr.description: arithmetic, or an aggregate over the rows: sum([Amount]), count(), avg(price), sum(qty * price) * 1.08

label.description: what the figure is, e.g. "invoice total"

tolerance.description: accept a difference up to this (decimal string, e.g. "0.01"); default 0

where.description: filters for this claim only, on top of the top-level where

value.description: text; a list for "in"; numbers as decimal strings

csv.description: the data as CSV text with a header row (instead of rows)

dateFormat.description: how to read slash dates like 03/04/2026: mdy (US) or dmy; ISO dates (2026-03-04, with or without a time) are always read. Default iso

rows.description: the data as JSON objects, one per row (up to 10000). Numbers as decimal strings are safest; JSON numbers are accepted

strictNumbers.description: true: refuse any cell that is not a plain decimal (no $, commas, %, or text in number columns). Default false: those are read and every change is reported

where.description: keep only rows matching ALL of these: eq, ne, gt, gte, lt, lte (numeric when both sides are numbers), contains (case-insensitive), in (list), empty, not_empty

value.description: text; a list for "in"; numbers as decimal strings

name: verify_answer
title: Check numbers before you send them (correct / wrong + the right value)
